items.title: MCMC probes Threads content insulting Negri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negri Sembilan. MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. MCMC is also examining how the content was disseminated across social media platforms and will work with relevant enforcement agencies should other offences under existing laws warrant action.

items.title: 4 Indonesians jailed for using fake passport stamps
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Four Indonesians were sentenced to five months' jail each by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to using fake stamps on their passports when entering Malaysia. All four pleaded guilty before judge Zulkpli Abdullah. They comprised 24 Indonesians, two Bangladeshis, two Myanmar nationals and one Vietnamese.

items.title: Kuching, Samarahan and Serian record unhealthy API readings as haze lingers over Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 18 — Kuching, Samarahan and Serian recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm today. According to the Natural Resource and Environment Board (NREB) website, Serian recorded the highest reading at 155, followed by Kuching 154 and Samarahan 148. Seventeen districts recorded moderate levels.

items.title: Nearly 11pct of screened Kelantan toddlers found stunted
items.summary: Kelantan Health Department director Dr Kasuadi Hussin said screenings conducted across 10 districts found that 9.8 per cent of the children were underweight, 10.9 per cent were stunted, 0.3 per cent were not fully immunised and 9.6 per cent had not received exclusive breastfeeding. Dr Kasuadi said being underweight could result from several factors, including insufficient food intake, calorie deficiency and unhealthy dietary habits, such as excessive consumption of junk food. "Children's health problems can be detected early through screenings.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Russia attacked Ukrainian energy sector 76 times in past week
items.summary: KYIV: Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors dozens of times in the week since US President Donald Trump announced a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday. Zelenskyy also predicted even more US sanctions relief. Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Najib house arrest rules in final drafting stage
items.summary: BESUT: The Prisons Department is in the final stages of drafting rules and conditions for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said the department, which is responsible for implementing Pardons Board decisions, had received a letter from the board's secretariat setting out the decision and related conditions. Saifuddin said the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat also stated that the Prisons Department could set any appropriate conditions.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning in 10 states, 2 FTs until 6pm
items.summary: MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang. In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.

items.title: E-commerce Bill to be tabled in March
items.summary: KUANTAN: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, will be tabled at the first parliamentary sitting next year. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the draft was ready and being revised. Fuziah also said 1,862 entrepreneurs had received assistance under the retail access programme from 2023 to October this year.

items.title: 'Never seen anything like it': Mass looting grips Paris
items.summary: SMASHING shop windows and snatching boxes of goods, looters in Paris poured into stores across the capital on Saturday, facing no resistance from authorities as nationwide protests degenerated into violence. From a small jewellery shop across the street, they took antique clocks. The CGT union, which took part, said 800,000 people participated.

items.title: Melaka election: Nine seats may see new faces
items.summary: AYER KEROH: At least nine sitting state assemblymen in Melaka could be dropped ahead of the upcoming state election, paving the way for fresh faces. Seats expected to see changes include Kuala Linggi, Rembia, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pengkalan Batu, Kesidang, Bemban, Serkam, and Sungai Rambai. In Pengkalan Batu, incumbent Datuk Kalsom Nordin faces uncertainty.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang. In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.

items.title: QR payment charges from Nov 1 claim is fake, says MOF
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Finance Ministry (MOF) today dismissed as false claims that service charges for quick response (QR) code payments would be introduced on Nov 1, as stated in a viral poster. In a Facebook post, the ministry said that no official announcement had been made about imposing QR code payment service charges, as the poster claimed. "The public is advised not to believe or share the poster claiming that QR payment service charges will be introduced on Nov 1, 2026, as the information is false," the statement said.

items.title: Pakatan finalises Melaka seat allocation but no deal yet with other parties, says PKR sec-gen
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to reach any concrete agreement on possible political cooperation with other parties for the November 14 Melaka state election. Datuk Fuziah Salleh, who is Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general, said, however, that seat-allocation negotiations among its three component parties — PKR, DAP and Amanah — had been finalised. She said PH was expected to contest more than 20 state seats, with nine allocated to PKR.

items.title: Two Saudi pilots killed in helicopter crash near Yemen border
items.summary: RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis on Sunday said two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the Iran-backed group said it shot the aircraft down. "An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the Ministry of National Guard crashed inside Saudi territory in Najran Region due to a technical malfunction," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency. Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.

items.title: Pangkor hit by flash floods in nine areas
items.summary: IPOH: Flash floods triggered by more than two hours of continuous heavy rain early today affected nine areas on Pangkor Island. The Perak Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the affected areas included Kampung Sungai Pinang Besar, Kampung Masjid, Kampung Teluk Kecil, Kampung Hussin, Teluk Gedung and Kampung Tengah. Other affected locations were the Rumah Murah area, Taman Pangkor Mutiara and Taman Sri Pangkor.

items.title: HRD Corp training grant applications surge after system reforms, says Ramanan
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The surge in Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications reflects the positive impact of measures taken to streamline its implementation system, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. It takes considerable time, and we thank the entire HRD Corp team for their dedication to carrying out these improvements,” he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp ‘Pocket Talk’ Roadshow: From Policy to the People here today. Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Aziz.

items.title: Hajiji recalls mother borrowing RM15 for exam fees as he vows poverty will not define Sabah children
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — Ensuring that poverty does not determine the fate of Sabah’s children or stand in the way of their progress has become a personal mission and commitment for Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Education is what can lift our children out of poverty. Driven by this commitment, he said he had ensured that the state government increased the allocation for the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) to RM155 million in 2026, up from RM55 million in 2021, to fund the education of students from underprivileged backgrounds.

items.title: Graduate salary floor must balance pay and jobs, economists say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed mandatory minimum starting salary for graduates should reflect job responsibilities, skills and productivity, while balancing higher wages against employers' ability to sustain recruitment, economists said. Its minister, Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, said the guidelines would provide employers and workers with a reference for basic starting salaries based on occupations, educational qualifications and skills. He said the government should consider employers' financial capacity, particularly among small and medium enterprises (SMEs), before making the proposed salary requirements compulsory.

items.title: Malaysians recount tense moments caught in Paris riots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian caught in Paris riots yesterday recounted tense moments when a mob of rioters left him trapped in traffic. Ozil Zainal, in a post on Threads, said he was driving into Paris after finding that traffic heading into the city was relatively light. Security personnel, including firefighters and ambulances, were seen rushing to the scene of the riots," said Ozil, adding that the riots had destroyed a lot of public property.

items.title: Malaysia considers helicopters, water-bombing aircraft to fight Indonesia fires
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Malaysia is considering deploying helicopters and water bombers to assist Indonesia in combating raging forest fires across the republic. He said the assistance under consideration includes deploying helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to support firefighting operations in affected areas. On Friday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had said Malaysia stands ready to assist Indonesia following President Prabowo Subianto's decision to accept assistance offers from neighbouring countries.

items.title: Unesco status alone won’t save silat if youth turn away, says Perak MB
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco) recognition of silat as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity does not guarantee its survival if younger generations increasingly distance themselves from training, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said. “We may have a proud silat heritage, but if young people turn away from the training arena, fewer will truly master and appreciate the art,” he said. Saarani said Malaysia has more than 150 identified silat styles, with the martial art declared a National Heritage in 2009 before gaining Unesco recognition as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019.

items.title: One night away, family returns to flood-hit home in Bukit Mertajam
items.summary: Ab Ghani Abdullah, 49, said he and his family had returned to Perlis on Friday to spend the night. "While I was sleeping at the village, I received a call from a friend who told me the water had risen around the house," he said when met at the temporary relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Seri Penanti here today. He said he and his family rushed back and arrived around 10pm last night, but had to register at the relief centre as the road to his house was still under about one metre of water.

items.title: ‘We cannot sit back’: Malaysia offers aircraft to fight Indonesia forest fires despite dangerously poor visibility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysia cannot afford to stand by as raging forest fires in Indonesia send thick haze across the region, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today, as the country offered to deploy helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help contain the blazes. But Mohamad warned that dangerously poor visibility, reportedly below 50m in affected areas, could hamper aerial firefighting operations and put pilots at risk. Thick smoke was also preventing aircraft from operating safely.

items.title: Check API readings to assess air quality amid haze, says DoE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public has been advised to refer to official Air Pollutant Index (API) readings to determine actual air quality rather than relying on surrounding conditions alone. Department of Environment (DoE) deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said API readings were based on measurements of air pollutants taken using specialised equipment. She said thick-looking haze did not necessarily indicate high levels of air pollution, as visibility was also affected by weather, humidity and the refraction of light by particles in the atmosphere.

items.title: Anwar approves RM30m to resurface 600 roads in Perak, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved a special allocation of RM30 million to resurface 600 roads in residential areas across Perak, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. “In conjunction with the Perak DAP Convention, I announced on behalf of the Prime Minister a special allocation of RM30 million for road resurfacing works in residential areas across the state. He said this while speaking at the 24th Perak DAP Annual Convention, officiated by DAP Secretary-General Anthony Loke here today.

items.title: AI-generated nude images of schoolgirls: Five police reports lodged
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Five police reports have been lodged over the circulation of AI-generated nude images of female students at a secondary school here, with more than 300 students reportedly affected. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the reports were lodged by parents between Aug 20 and 23 over the distribution of images allegedly featuring the faces of female students. Ng said the five police reports were lodged on Aug 20, including one by the parents of the student who found the phone.

items.title: Malaysia's diversified economy, fiscal buffers to cushion external shocks: Amir Hamzah
items.summary: BANGKOK: Malaysia's diversified economy, resilient export markets and stronger fiscal buffers will help cushion external shocks and support its growth outlook for 2027, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said geopolitical tensions, shifting global trade patterns and economic uncertainty would remain key risks, but Malaysia is better positioned to withstand disruptions after adapting to previous crises, including the Russia-Ukraine war and ongoing trade tensions. Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's economic base has broadened beyond commodities and oil and gas to include electrical and electronics, semiconductors, data centres and advanced manufacturing, reducing its reliance on any single sector.

items.title: Long Lellang heli crash: Doctor's husband wants final report expedited
items.summary: MIRI: The husband of a medical officer killed in the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, has urged authorities to expedite the release of the final investigation report. Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, whose wife Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin was among five killed in the Sept 8 crash, said findings released so far remain preliminary. On Friday, a preliminary report released by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) revealed that the safety investigation is ongoing, with factual information gathered so far at an initial stage.

items.title: JD Vance has yet to decide on 2028 US Presidential run
items.summary: ISTANBUL: US Vice President JD Vance said he has not decided whether to run for president in 2028, acknowledging he could ultimately opt out despite being widely viewed as a leading contender to succeed President Donald Trump, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing CBS News. Trump has called Vance his "most likely" Republican successor. Vance also defended the administration's economic and foreign policies, blaming former President Joe Biden's administration for neglecting manufacturing while acknowledging that reversing its decline would take time.

items.title: Malaysians in Italy, France advised to avoid protest sites
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Malaysians travelling to Italy and France have been advised to avoid student protest sites amid concerns over their safety and the risk of arrest by the authorities. However, he advised Malaysians to remain vigilant and stay away from areas where demonstrations were taking place. "There are no travel restrictions at present, but we advise Malaysians to stay away from areas where student demonstrations are taking place daily.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to be tabled next year to regulate online transactions, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament at the first meeting next year to strengthen the regulation of online transactions, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh. Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme, which combines training and business matching, has helped 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to October this year. She said the programme comprised 38 training series and 21 business matching series, involving 103 local brands and 552 stock-keeping units (SKUs).

items.title: Regional anxiety and historical echoes follow Japan's militarisation
items.summary: LETTER: Japan is on the road to full militarisation. Its military budget has exceeded nine trillion yen (US$68 billion), hitting the target of two per cent of GDP, though lagging behind the United States (US$1 trillion) and China (US$340 billion). Japan has overhauled its post-World War II (WW2) defence export policies, lifting strict limits on export of lethal weapons.

items.title: Perak maintains ban on outdoor school activities despite improving API readings, says exco
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — Although Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at four monitoring stations in Perak have shown a decline, outdoor school activities remain prohibited due to the current haze situation. State Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said schools in the state were operating as usual, while teaching and learning activities must be conducted indoors. He said the ban covers outdoor activities, such as camping and sports, while motivational programmes must also be held indoors.

items.title: Nepal seeks legal changes to expedite death certificates for 54 missing Malaysians
items.summary: MELAKA: Nepal is seeking to amend its laws to expedite the issuance of death certificates for 54 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following floods and landslides in the country in August. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Nepal's current laws require a waiting period of up to three years before death certificates can be issued for people who remain missing after a disaster. Mohamad said the certificates were needed by the victims' families to settle related matters, including dealings with banks and insurance companies.

items.title: Storm, flash floods damage 23 houses in Pendang
items.summary: Pendang Civil Defence officer Yuslina Yusoff said the first report was received at 5.30pm before six Malaysian Civil Defence Force personnel were dispatched to the affected areas. She said strong winds damaged the roofs of four houses in Kampung Bukit Pak Pom and three in Kampung Lahar Tunjang. Meanwhile, Yuslina said flash floods affected 16 houses in two other villages, involving 13 homes in Kampung Baru, Mukim Padang Peliang, and three in Kampung Titi Akar, Mukim Padang Kerbau.

items.title: Foreign minister: Nepal seeks legal amendments to expedite death certificates for 54 Malaysians
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 18 — The Nepalese government is seeking to amend the country’s laws to expedite the issuance of death certificates for 54 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following floods and landslides that hit the country in August. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Nepal’s existing laws require a waiting period of up to three years before death certificates can be issued for individuals who remain unaccounted for after a disaster. He said the death certificates are necessary for the victims’ families to manage related affairs, including matters involving banks and insurance companies.

items.title: Haze persists in KL despite rain as winds bring more pollution, says DoE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze continues to affect the capital despite recent rain, as winds carry smoke and pollutants into the country while high humidity and water vapour contribute to poor visibility. The Batu Muda and Cheras monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 156 and 155 respectively at noon today. "Winds are still carrying haze into the country, causing API readings to remain high in most areas," she told the New Straits Times.

items.title: Two killed, including 6-year-old, when truck drives through Kansas youth football match: Police
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A truck drove into a youth football match in Wichita, Kansas, leaving a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man dead, and 10 others hospitalised with traumatic injuries, police said on Saturday. The two people killed were pronounced dead at the scene, he said. The injured include two youths aged 5, two aged 8, a 9-year-old and five adults, police said.

items.title: Tok Mat: N. Sembilan crisis won’t disrupt BN’s Melaka state election machinery
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 18 — The crisis in Negeri Sembilan is not expected to affect Barisan Nasional’s (BN) preparations for the Melaka state election next month, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said the key was to ensure that strategies drawn up by the party leadership were effectively implemented by its election machinery to secure victory, adding that good strategies not implemented will also cause plans to fail. In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Malaysians advised to postpone non-essential travel to France amid protests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysians have been advised to consider postponing non-essential travel to France until the situation improves amid ongoing demonstrations in major cities across the country. The Embassy of Malaysia in Paris has issued an advisory urging Malaysians in France to exercise caution and remain vigilant. “While travel to France remains unrestricted, Malaysians are advised to consider postponing non-essential travel until the situation improves,” the ministry said.

items.title: Vietnam signs free trade deal with four European nations
items.summary: HANOI: Vietnam and four European nations outside the EU signed a free trade agreement in Hanoi on Sunday, seeking to diversify their markets as US tariffs disrupt global commerce. Vietnam said the agreement showed the parties' resolve to "reinforce the rules-based trading system amid continued volatility in the global economy", according to a government statement. Vietnam and EFTA concluded negotiations in July, more than a decade after the free trade talks officially began in 2012.

items.title: Negri Sembilan crisis will not affect BN's Melaka polls preparations – Tok Mat
items.summary: MELAKA: The political situation in Negri Sembilan is not expected to affect Barisan Nasional's preparations for the Melaka election next month, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said the key is ensuring that strategies drawn up by party leadership are effectively executed by the election machinery to secure victory, noting that good strategies fail without proper implementation. "We can draw up an excellent strategy that looks very good on paper, with many voters identified or categorised as BN's fixed supporters," he said.

items.title: Police hunt Honda Accord driver after van driver knocked down in PJ
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Police are tracking down the driver of a black Honda Accord after a van driver was knocked down following a road dispute here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received a report from the van driver at 6.22pm yesterday. "The van driver stopped his vehicle and asked the car driver to get out.

items.title: DAP reps who fail performance targets risk losing candidacy in GE17, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — DAP representatives must meet strict key performance indicators (KPIs) or risk losing their candidacy in the next general election (GE17), party secretary-general Anthony Loke said today. According to Berita Harian , Loke stressed that all DAP lawmakers must serve with integrity, discipline and commitment. Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming was also present at the event.

items.title: Authorities capture 12-foot crocodile at Teluk Nipah beach in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 18 — A 12-foot crocodile was captured at Teluk Nipah beach in Buntal here last Thursday. The Civil Defence Force Kuching (APM Kuching), in a Facebook post, said its response team, together with personel from the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) and Nemo Hunter team, carried out the operation to capture the crocodile. Meanwhile, in his Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the capture followed a public report from a 55-year-old man.

items.title: Warisan leader: Tawau residents endure water disruptions of up to two weeks, urges govt to act
items.summary: TAWAU, Oct 18 — Residents in several areas here have been forced to endure prolonged water supply disruptions lasting up to two weeks, prompting calls for the state government and Sabah Water Department to take immediate and comprehensive action. He said residents in Bandar Sri Indah had reportedly experienced water supply disruptions for 10 days, while those in Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai and Taman Millennium had faced disruptions lasting up to two weeks. Residents should not have to endure days or even weeks without a reliable water supply,” he said.

items.title: WhatsApp scam: Miri man loses RM97,000 after fraudsters use his profile to dupe wife
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 18 — A man here reported a loss of RM97,000 after fraudsters allegedly used his identity and profile picture on WhatsApp to deceive his wife into transferring funds into third-party accounts. Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said according to a report filed yesterday, the victim’s wife received a WhatsApp message on Oct 16 from an unknown number displaying her husband’s profile. “She then made two online money transfers using a company account, amounting to RM48,000 and RM49,000 respectively, into two different bank accounts,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Budget 2027: Higher STR, SARA allocations help recipients plan spending, say beneficiaries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The RM16 billion allocation for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) financial aid under Budget 2027 has been described as a vital lifeline for recipients managing their monthly expenses. When tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the increased allocation allows nine million STR recipients to receive SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year. “This assistance helps reduce my monthly expenses significantly.

items.title: MediAsas plan to offer financial, health safety net to Malaysia’s M40, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia’s middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges. Earlier, the Ministry of Finance announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan).

items.title: No, QR payments are not getting a service charge from Nov 1, says Finance Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Finance Ministry today debunked a poster claiming that QR payments will start carrying a service charge from November 1. The ministry said in a Facebook post today that the poster, which circulated under the headline “Top news today: QR to start service charge on Nov 1”, contains untrue information. “There is no official announcement on service charges for QR as claimed in the poster,” it said.

items.title: Sahabat Madani Selangor to boost youth participation in community service, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Sahabat Madani Selangor initiative aims to strengthen youth participation in volunteerism and community service to support local communities. Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the initiative was a continuation of the Sahabat Madani programme launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Penang last August. “Sahabat Madani provides an ideal platform for young people to participate in such programmes and contribute to community development,” he told Bernama after launching the Rentap Pandan Madani 2026 Muay Thai Championship at the Muhibbah Complex here last night.

items.title: Civil marriage solemnisation does not usurp role of religious leaders, says JPN
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The solemnisation of civil marriages by authorised parties under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164) cannot be equated with the performance of religious rituals or regarded as taking over the role of religious leaders. The National Registration Department (NRD) said the function was a responsibility carried out in accordance with the laws of the country. Act 164 empowers appointed Registrars of Marriages and Assistant Registrars of Marriages to solemnise and register civil marriages.

items.title: Border agency praises late officer Norhazwani’s dedication, pledges family support
items.summary: TUMPAT, Oct 18 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, on Thursday, was described as a hardworking and dedicated officer. AKPS Deputy Director-General (Operations) SAC Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M. Nasir said Norhazwani, who joined the agency on July 1 after transferring from the Customs Department, had performed well and was committed to her duties. He said Norhazwani frequently worked overtime and had two children who still required attention and family support.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Low Zi Yu-Genevie Lim on ending Malaysia’s 34-year wait for badminton World Junior title
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national women’s junior doubles pair Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on their outstanding achievement in winning the title at the 2026 World Junior Badminton Championships in Cairo, Egypt. Congratulations to Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on winning the girls’ doubles title at the World Junior Badminton Championships. The historic win ended Malaysia’s 34-year wait for its maiden girls’ doubles title since the world junior meet was first held in 1992.

items.title: Anwar hails Siti Nurhaliza’s soulful Gema Bumantara concert as 63,000 braved rain to attend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin on her exceptional and soulful performance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara show last night. “It was a pleasure to enjoy Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza’s performance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara last night, which beautifully celebrated the rich artistic heritage of the Nusantara. Bravo, Datuk Seri Siti, and bravo to her dedicated fans.

items.title: Sister bars in-laws from attending funeral of border agency officer allegedly killed by husband, says they didn’t ask about children
items.summary: TUMPAT, Oct 18 — The family of Norhazwani Ibrahim, a 35-year-old border agency officer allegedly murdered by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, has refused to allow his parents and relatives to attend her funeral here, saying they cannot accept what he is accused of doing. The victim’s elder sister, Marlina, 46, told Utusan Malaysia that the family had also barred the husband’s relatives from visiting the deceased before her burial. Norhazwani had planned to visit the family again in December, Marlina said.

items.title: Khaled Nordin begins four-day working visit to Japan to strengthen defence ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin’s official working visit to Japan, which begins today, is expected to bring tangible benefits to the country’s defence while enhancing mutual understanding in addressing regional security challenges. Mohamed Khaled, who safely arrived at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, said key engagements during the visit include bilateral meetings with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. He said the visit woud also include a meeting with Japan’s Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA), as well as a visit to Japanese defence company, Toshiba.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN to unveil candidate list on Oct 28, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 18 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will announce the list of candidates who will contest in the Melaka State Election (PRN) on October 28, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Also present were Kedah Umno Liaison Body Chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid, Melaka MCA Chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong, and Tangga Batu Umno Division Chief Datuk Rais Yasin. The Election Commission (EC) has set polling day for the Melaka state election on November 14, while nomination day is set for October 31 and early voting on November 10.

items.title: Wrong Nani, wrong story: Presenter Nani Roc tells online sleuths she’s not in the khalwat story
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Presenter and influencer Nani Roslan has denied being the woman detained alongside former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad in a Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) raid last Thursday for alleged khalwat — a Syariah offence involving an unmarried Muslim man and woman found alone together in a secluded place or in close proximity. “I am not that woman. She also co-hosted the Lebih Masa podcast with Nik Nazmi, an arrangement she said ended on September 30.

items.title: Selangor studying retention ponds, drainage upgrades for Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang, says exco
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 18 — The Selangor state government is conducting a detailed study to identify critical locations for new retention ponds and drainage upgrades to address flash floods, particularly in urban areas. State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said the study would focus on areas requiring urgent solutions, including Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang. Izham said that besides constructing retention ponds and upgrading drainage systems, he had also proposed alternative flood mitigation measures, including a ‘water highway’ in the Klang Valley.
